consideration_and_rights: Dell 2016 Q3 Form 10-Q reports that each EMC share at the September 7, 2016 effective time was converted to $24.05 cash plus 0.11146 Dell Class V common share, with cash instead of any fractional Class V share.

The Class V shares were designed to track Dell’s economic interest in the Class V Group (then including about 65% of Dell’s VMware economic interest); the filing states this was tracking-stock exposure, not direct ownership or recourse to those group assets. The market price was not guaranteed to track that interest.

Dell’s 2019 Form 10-K reports Class V was exchanged on December 28, 2018 for either $120 cash per share subject to a $14 billion aggregate cash cap, or 1.8066 Dell Class C shares. This later conversion is part of the original entitlement chain, not a value assigned here.
events.dividends: The two saved Dell filings reviewed here do not establish whether a Class V dividend was paid over the full holding interval. VMware dividend context in the 2016 filing is not proof of all later Dell Class V distributions. Unknown.
